_note: PURGED AND REBUILT 2026-08-23 (Ben): the hot file holds only the items of the earliest incomplete sprint - Sprint 16, the mercenary vertical slice (v0.1.15). Every item that existed before (530, ids <= BL-568) is snapshotted verbatim in archive/backlog-purged-2026-08-23.json and is NOT open work. New items name their sprint in `sprint`. File nothing here that the open sprint does not need; when the sprint closes, the next sprint's items are authored fresh against the authority docs. Ids never reuse.
Canonical backlog for Project Io — the authoritative METADATA index of every backlog item.
One item = one object in `items`.
STATUS (authoritative; JSON wins over any prose/glyph disagreement):
designed    (glyph ✓) — design settled, promote-ready.
design-owed (glyph ~) — design still owed; must be settled before promotion.
PRIORITY (ascending): F C B A S SSS.
F=deferred/parked, C=low, B=medium, A=important, S=high, SSS=do-immediately.
`parked:true` is the explicit flag for F-priority items.
DIFFICULTY (1-5): 1=~5min, 2=~20min, 3=~1h, 4=~3h, 5=~12h+ (break a 5 down).
SEQUENCING: `requires` lists BL-XXX ids of backlog items that must land first (supercedes the
old `waits_on` short_name list — v2 schema 2026-06-17). `blocked_on` names a truly-external
prerequisite with no backlog item (third-party dep, real-world gate). An item can be `designed`
and still have unmet `requires`. Both fields are nullable; [] means no dependencies.
WORKFLOW: a `designed` item is PROMOTED into REFINED.md and DELIVERED (see DELIVERY.md).
A `design-owed` item is DESIGNED first (prose settled in `design` field, status flipped).
When work lands, the item is RETAINED here under the terminal status `complete` with a
resolution/completion_note, and design propagates into the authority doc. (Convention updated
2026-07-04: terminal items were once removed; the tooling — gyre.py, progress counts — now
depends on them staying. Do not delete landed entries.)
(Terminal status normalised 2026-08-01: `complete` is the only one. `shipped` was a
synonym with no defined difference — written only by tools/session/ship_items.js and
apply_session_close.js, which now write `complete`; the six items carrying it were
converted. Readers still tolerate the old value, so nothing breaks on an old branch.)
DESIGN PROSE — the `design` field (policy updated 2026-06-17):
- ALL items: prose lives in the `design` field here, not in BACKLOG.md.
- NEW items: author prose here directly. No BACKLOG.md body.
- LEGACY items (pre-2026-06-17): `design: "@BACKLOG.md"` means prose is still in markdown.
Migrate to this field on first edit (design settle or promotion) — do not wait for promotion.
On migration: write prose here, replace the BACKLOG.md body with a tombstone line.
- ON PROMOTION into REFINED.md: delete any remaining BACKLOG.md body (if not yet migrated).
- BACKLOG.md therefore only drains, never grows, and is deleted once empty.
- For designs with rich tables use markdown in the `design` string (tables render fine).
- `design: "@<doc>"` is also valid as a pointer to an authority doc when prose lives there.
VERSION GOAL (policy added 2026-07-08): every NEW item names which version it is FOR via the
`version_goal` field — the minor it targets ("v0.0.9"), the next one ("v0.1.0"), or
"post-v0.1.0" for anything beyond the prototype's remaining arc (see ROADMAP.md for the
live version sequence and themes). This is a goal, not a promise — it may slip a version at
re-sequencing, same as priority. Legacy items predating this policy are not backfilled; treat
a missing `version_goal` as "unset (legacy)", not as "post-v0.1.0".
ARCHIVE — the hot/cold split (policy added 2026-08-02):
This file is the METADATA INDEX and is read ACROSS items far more often than INTO one.
So when an item lands, its narrative fields — design, resolution, completion_note,
progress_note — MOVE OUT to docs/development/archive/backlog-design-<quarter>.json.
The item keeps `design: "@<that path>"` (the pointer form blessed above) plus an
`archived` field naming the cold file. This is the authority time-slice made physical:
backlog.json owns the item while it is open; the cold store and the subject authority
doc own it once it has landed.
- Run it: tools/session/archive_designs.js (Delivery close step, after ship_items.js).
- Read it back: tools/session/backlog_query.js --full, or backlog_view.js — both resolve
the pointer transparently, so an archived item reads exactly like a hot one.
- Reverse it: archive_designs.js --restore [BL-XXX ...]. Nothing is ever deleted.
- AMEND A LANDED ITEM'S PROSE IN THE COLD FILE, not here — the hot file has no copy.
- backlog_lint.js FAILS on an `archived` pointer with no record behind it, and WARNS
when frozen history climbs back over 30% of this file.
AUTHOR (policy added 2026-08-22): items may carry an `author` field naming who
proposed the item (e.g. "Joe"). Informational only — no effect on status, priority,
or workflow. Nullable; missing/null means unattributed (legacy items). Design
brainstorms that haven't yet become a backlog item live in docs/development/design/.

items.title: A province has a holder, and a won battle moves it
condition_set can say 'province P held by the subject', and a contract template is an authored Lua row
Nations field force: a garrison per nation, and a battle can have a nation on one side
A nation derives a contract offer from its budget, and the contracted_force line takes a subject
The mercenary contract: accept an offer with a named force, evaluate it each tick, pay or fail
One observed instance of every contract terminal state, conserved and replayable
items.summary: CONTRACTS.md demands one observed instance of each terminal state; no harness in the tree can observe any. This is the headless proof the slice rests on, in the procurement_harness.cpp pattern (fixture world, scripted verbs, bit-exact goldens).
items.design:
## Cases

M1 offer issued by a threatened nation; M2 accept with a valid force, deposit moves client->contractor and conserves exactly; M3 take-template completed on a decisive battle (BL-569/BL-571 fixtures), remainder paid; M4 hold-template failed on the first lost tick, escrow returned, `contract_failed` folded and reputation lower than after a cancel; M5 abandon; M6 two runs from one seed hash-identical across all of the above; M7 save/load mid-contract round-trips. Name the harness in the verifier-headless skill.

items.title: A unit is visible on the Planetary canvas and can be ordered to march
The Contracts ledger: offers in, accept with a force, active and past contracts
items.summary: The offer has to reach a human. No contract, offer, procurement or budget surface exists; the decision feed prints 'contract #n' and that is the whole story. A fold-out ledger in the nav rail with three views - Offers (client, province, fee, deadline, the client's visible garrison), Active (predicate text from condition_text, ticks left, committed force), History (terminal state, paid) - and an Accept flow that is a unit picker over the player's uncommitted units.
items.design:
## Work

1. Rail slot + `show_contracts_ledger`; the toggle rule (re-clicking the active tab closes).
2. Offers view rows; the Accept press opens the force picker (owned, uncommitted units with strength); confirm dispatches `accept_offer`. Decline is local (the offer stays until expiry - refusable, not dismissable).
3. Active view: `condition_text` line, deadline countdown, an Abandon press with the reputation cost shown.
4. Question-log entries (the question each view answers); ACTIONS.json ledger-family entries.
5. The fog rule: an offer is visible only if the target body is at least Known (DISCOVERY.md) - CONTRACTS.md's settled answer.

items.title: spectator_determinism's R2 stops asserting a toolchain-specific golden
items.summary: R2's byte-identity row asserts a golden recorded from an MSVC build, and the harness says in its own comment that the value is toolchain-specific because float clearing arithmetic differs under g++. So every cloud or Linux session opens on one red row that is not a regression, which teaches sessions to discount reds - the one thing a harness must never do.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-548)

Replace R2's byte-identity with a **same-run A/B: spectated vs unspectated in one process, which needs no golden at all.** The compile-time toolchain guard and the per-toolchain golden were both considered and rejected.

## Measured baseline (this container, g++ 13.3, 2026-08-23)

Built with `node tools/verify/build_harness.js spectator_determinism`. Exactly ONE failure:
R2 byte-identity, `golden=344A9FE48306E93A observed=B4D09255AF346008` - the same observed value NR-536 and NR-484 independently recorded, so the world is reproducible and the golden is simply from another toolchain. Every other row passes: the prohibition, both reproducibility rows, all four R1 A/B seat rows, both cadence rows, and R3's three rows including 'spectating moves the world'.

## The design problem to solve first

The golden carries a CROSS-TIME claim - 'the unspectated path is byte-identical to what it produced before BL-409 existed'. No same-run comparison can make that claim, because nothing in one process knows what the pre-BL-409 world was. So the replacement must assert a DIFFERENT property, and the item is not done until that property is one with teeth. Note R3 already asserts the spectated and unspectated hashes DIFFER, so a naive 'A/B' row would restate R3.

The property worth having is that **admitting the player corp is additive, not disruptive**: the spectator guard must not perturb anything except by the player's own actions. Two candidate shapes, to be settled while building:

1. **Rivals agree until the player first acts.** Record the tick of the player's first action in the spectated rollout; assert every rival's decision stream is identical between the played and spectated runs for every tick before it. Catches a guard that perturbs iteration order, RNG draw count or any accumulator merely by evaluating the player corp.
2. **A spectated run whose player takes zero actions is byte-identical to the played run.** Stronger and simpler to state, but needs a way to admit the corp while refusing its candidates, which is a new hook.

Shape 1 needs no new seam and is the recommended first cut. R1 already proves the weaker neighbour of it ('admitting the player shifts NO rival's cadence slot').

## Work

1. Author the replacement row(s) per the shape chosen; DELETE `k_unspectated_golden` and its ~70 lines of bless provenance, or keep the constant as a REPORTED value that asserts nothing.
2. Prove the new row can fail (DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md, mutation step): perturb the unspectated path from inside the spectating branch and confirm it reds.
3. `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` currently sends the reader to the harness provenance log for the current constant. If the constant goes, that sentence is rewritten to name the A/B instead - the rule's CLAIM (the flag defaults false, an ordinary session is unaffected) is unchanged and stays.
4. Run under BOTH toolchains before closing. That is the whole point.

## Not in scope

Re-blessing any other harness's goldens. `ai_skill_harness` self-declares stale bands and is a separate call.

items.title: A headless harness can measure the configuration the game actually ships
items.summary: make_hard_coded_world reads two Lua-authored inputs a headless harness cannot load - scripts/works.lua and scripts/world_gen.lua - because the TUs excluded from a headless build are exactly the Lua ones. history_sim.cpp gates build_work on a non-empty works registry, so the harness scores a verb set the game does not have.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-558)

**Extend the live-Lua pattern to the harnesses that need it.** Re-authoring the two content files as C++ defaults was rejected (it creates the second source of truth), as was labelling the divergence and living with it.

## Why it is priority A

This is the same failure mode BL-462 named and the third instance of it: a check that looks like it measures the product and does not. Its current victim is the war-rate question - every history harness scores a polity that cannot choose `build_work`, because the works registry it reads is empty.

## Work

1. `tier_margin` and `player_seed_sweep` already do this: they link `recipe_registry.cpp` + `src/scripting/lua_state.cpp` + `lua54` and load the shipped scripts. Lift that into a reusable CMake helper rather than a fourth hand-declared target - the file's own comment records that hand-picked source lists rot, and it has three of them already.
2. Point the history harnesses at it, so `works.lua` and `world_gen.lua` reach generation.
3. Re-measure the war-rate table afterward and say plainly whether the 11-of-32 silent-world figure survives loading the real works table.
4. `tools/verify/build_harness.js` refuses live-Lua harnesses by name; extend its refusal list, or teach it the Lua link line if that is cheap.

## Not in scope

Re-tuning any history-sim weight. Measure first.

items.title: A harness cannot join the ctest gate without naming its timeout tier
items.summary: The CMake glob registers tools/verify/*.cpp automatically, so a new harness enters the routine gate silently at the 60 s default. road_reach_census and rival_military_seeding_harness are in neither IO_TEST_LONG_HARNESSES nor IO_TEST_SWEEP_HARNESSES today.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-402 / NR-259)

**Make the glob refuse an unlisted harness, so every new one names its tier deliberately.** The softer options - just move the two, or add a checklist line - were both rejected.

## Why

This is exactly how `player_seed_sweep` spent its whole life red: a 60 s timeout on a 69 s tool, invisible because a ctest Timeout looks like nothing. A default that silently mis-classifies is worse than one that stops the build and asks.

## Work

1. Add a third list - `IO_TEST_DEFAULT_HARNESSES` - and make the foreach `message(FATAL_ERROR)` on any globbed harness in none of the three, naming the file and the three lists. The error text is the whole feature: it must tell the author what to do, not just that something is wrong.
2. Classify the current set, `road_reach_census` and `rival_military_seeding_harness` included (both are census-class and both are measured multi-world runs, so LONG at minimum - measure before choosing).
3. Note the cost honestly in the skill: a NEW harness now fails the configure until listed. That is the intent, and it needs to be discoverable or it will read as a broken build.

## Verification note

This is a CMake change and a configure is the only thing that tests it. It was deliberately NOT authored in the 2026-08-23 review session, which could not run `cmake -B build` (FetchContent is refused by that container's egress policy) - authoring a build-system change that cannot be configured is the NR-240 failure mode.

items.title: --autostart-play terminates unattended and the exit path is unnamed
items.summary: --autostart-play works interactively but has ended on its own three times when launched from a background shell - at roughly 20 s, 34 s and ~60 s, exit code 0, no crash log, no exception, output simply stopping after the warm-start.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-256)

**Instrument the three exit paths** - a few lines, and it distinguishes the two hypotheses in one run each.

## Work

1. One `printf` on each of the three paths that can end the run loop, each naming itself.
2. Launch once from a real terminal and once from a background shell. That separates (a) a real in-app exit condition from (b) something about the detached shell - a closed stdin, a lost window handle, a signal.
3. Fix what it names, or record what it names if the fix is larger.

The instrumentation is the deliverable even if the cause turns out to be environmental: a flag that ends silently at exit code 0 is indistinguishable from one that worked.

items.title: The Profitability page says which of its numbers are estimates
items.summary: The page's 'Net, 6 mo.' chart is a smooth deterministic series anchored to the live estimate, because no per-building profit history is recorded anywhere in the simulation. The player reads a plausible line as history.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-248 / NR-249)

**Label it on screen as an estimate until history exists.** Recording real per-building history was considered and is the larger item; removing the chart and leaving it unmarked were both rejected.

## Work

1. Mark the 'Net, 6 mo.' series on the Profitability page as an estimate, in the chart's own chrome rather than a tooltip - a label a player must hover to find does not undo the impression the line makes.
2. The same idiom, and the same treatment, applies to `draw_building_workforce_page`'s pre-existing placeholder trend graph. Both, or neither - they are the same lie twice.
3. SELECTION.md states what the page shows and which parts are derived rather than recorded.

## Not in scope

Per-building profit history, and any revenue sub-breakdown. `building_profit` tracks four numbers and the pooled market resists attributing even the one revenue figure per building - that constraint is real and is not what this item is about. A UI requirement needs a live click, not just a capture.

items.title: PHANTOMS.md dissolves into per-doc 'What is absent' sections
items.summary: The phantom register is a document class nothing in the corpus owns - a list of things with no owner, overlapping NEEDS_REVIEW (open calls), backlog.json (work) and MILITARY.md's own per-doc absent-list, which is the pattern it generalises. It is written as transient and nothing says who prunes it.
items.design:
## Ben's ruling, 2026-08-23 (NR-513)

**Dissolve it into per-doc 'What is absent' sections, and make the scan a periodic check rather than a document.** Keeping it as a transient scan output, and growing it a query tool, were both rejected.

## Work

1. Each of the 322 lines' rows moves into the authority doc that owns its subject, as a 'What is absent' section on MILITARY.md's model. A row whose subject has NO owning doc is the interesting case: it is the one that needs a doc, and it should be reported rather than dropped.
2. Delete PHANTOMS.md once every row has a home.
3. The scan becomes a session verb, not an artifact - name where it lives in DELIVERY.md.

## Watch for

A 'What is absent' section is a statement about the DESIGN, not about build status - io-standing-rules.md, doc state-independence. 'Nothing owns how X is priced' is a design fact and belongs; 'X is not built yet' is a backlog fact and does not. This distinction is the whole difficulty of the item and is why it is a 3.
